chunks: From him, from Ibn Faddal, from Ibn Bukayr, from Ubayd ibn Zur'arah, who said:
I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'Indeed, the maternal siblings do not exclude the mother from the one-third share.'

key_terms.الْإِخْوَةَ مِنَ الْأُمِّ: Maternal siblings (siblings sharing the same mother)
key_terms.يَحْجُبُونَ: Exclude / prevent from receiving a share

ai.seo_question: Do maternal siblings exclude the mother from her one-third inheritance share?
ai.summary: This hadith from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the distinction between *hujb* (exclusion) and *haram* (blocking) in Shia inheritance law, specifically noting that maternal siblings (*ikhwat min al-umm*) do not block the mother from her fixed one-third share. Unlike paternal siblings who reduce the mother’s share to one-sixth, maternal siblings are considered *habib* (non-excluding) relatives in this context, preserving the mother’s full entitlement. This ruling underscores the Shia emphasis on the mother’s elevated status and distinct lineage rights compared to the father’s side of the family.
